red_flags: Owner with no real estate history fronting a deal an experienced party runs
Track record borrowed from a partner who is not on the chart
Third party pays the deposit or cash to close
Guarantor cannot explain the project in a call
documents: Bank statements and source of cash to close
Settlement statements and deeds for the track record
rows.control: Chart to natural persons and verify each 20% owner (CORE-KYC-02, -08); verify experience by settlement statement or public record (CORE-BOR-15); straw or nominee owner and unrelated third-party funds stop the file for the BSA officer (CORE-KYC-07).

mcq.stem: Exhibit: Maple Run track record listing 7 flips; one settlement statement shows Dana owned 15% of a deal. Which count does policy allow?
mcq.key: 6 projects; the 15% deal fails the 20% ownership test (CORE-BOR-15).
distractors: 7 projects, as listed.
0, because one entry is doubtful.
7, if Sam Okafor co-signs.

red_flags: Guarantor's ID, mail or utilities at the subject address
Lease to a relative or with a shared surname
No proof of the guarantor's other home
Cash-out for personal use
documents: Utility bills, credit report address history
rows.control: Certification before closing (CORE-BP-01); red flag stops the file and needs written evidence, with contradictions sent to the BSA officer (CORE-BP-02); cash-out majority-personal is declined (CORE-BP-04); lease to an unrelated tenant (RES-GEN-11).

mcq.stem: Exhibit: Maple Run month-11 lease to 'C. Reyes' and the guarantor's credit report showing the subject as a current address. What happens?
mcq.key: The file stops; contradicting evidence goes to the BSA officer, who alone clears it (CORE-BP-02).
distractors: Accept the lease; a lease is enough.
Raise the rate for consumer risk.
Ask Chris Reyes to sign the guaranty.

red_flags: Borrower or broker sends their own appraisal or names the appraiser
Comparables are newer, larger or in a different market
ARV per square foot far above the comparables
Pressure to 'hit a value'
documents: Lender-ordered appraisal and AMC engagement letter
rows.control: Appraisal ordered only through the lender's AMC from a certified appraiser (CORE-VAL-01); desk review of every appraisal (CORE-VAL-03); BPOs and AVMs as checks only (CORE-VAL-03, RES-GEN-06).

mcq.stem: Exhibit: a broker email attaching an 'updated ARV' of $575,000 for Maple Run, against the AMC's $520,000. What should the underwriter do?
mcq.key: Size on the AMC value and log the broker's pressure as a red flag (CORE-VAL-01).
distractors: Use $575,000; it is more recent.
Average the two values.
Order a BPO to break the tie.

rows.typology: Rapid flip chains (title chain and seasoning)
red_flags: Seller took title weeks ago at a much lower price
Related parties on both sides of prior sales
Assignment of contract with a large fee
No work done to explain the price jump
documents: Title commitment with 24-month chain of title
rows.control: A prior sale within 12 months at 20% or more below today's price or value stops the file for the BSA officer (CORE-KYC-07);title commitment review (CORE-CLS-01); DSCR value is the lesser of appraisal and cost basis if owned under 6 months (RES-DSCR-05).

mcq.stem: Exhibit: title chain showing the subject sold 4 months ago for $230,000; contract price now $300,000. Does a policy flag fire?
distractors: No: the gap is under 25%.
No: only the appraiser reviews prior sales.
No: the lookback covers refinances, not purchases.

red_flags: Rent roll income not seen in bank deposits
Many leases signed the same week at above-market rents
Tenant names repeat or match related parties
No security deposits held
documents: Three months of operating bank statements
rows.control: Rent roll must tie to bank deposits within 5% for the last 3 months (MF-GEN-04); underwritten income is the lesser of rent roll and trailing 3 months (MF-GEN-05); estoppels (COM-GEN-09).

mcq.stem: Cedar Court what-if: rent roll annualized $702,000 against deposits annualized $640,000 for three months. What does policy say?
mcq.key: It fails the 5% tie-out ($62,000 is 8.8% of $702,000), so income must be explained before underwriting (MF-GEN-04).
distractors: It passes; deposits are within 10%.
Use the rent roll; deposits lag.
Use GPR instead.

red_flags: Fonts, alignment or totals that do not foot
Round-number deposits just before application
Statement dates outside the 60-day window
Balances that differ from a verification of deposit
documents: Two most recent monthly bank statements
Direct bank verification or account-aggregation report
rows.control: Two most recent statements dated within 60 days of closing (CORE-BOR-13); conflicting documents stop the file for the BSA officer (CORE-KYC-07).
rows.policy_gap: No rule requires direct verification from the bank. Ask the owner whether to add one.

mcq.stem: Exhibit: Dana Reyes's statement showing a $95,000 ending balance, but the transaction lines add to $59,000. What is the next step?
mcq.key: Treat it as conflicting documents: stop the file and send it to the BSA officer (CORE-KYC-07).
distractors: Use the ending balance shown.
Use the average of the two figures.
Ask the borrower for a letter explaining it, then proceed.

red_flags: Contractor owned by the borrower or a relative
Appraiser named by the borrower or broker
Draw inspector paid by the borrower
Budget lines far above local costs
documents: Contractor licence, insurance and state business-entity record
Ownership chart cross-checked against the contractor
rows.control: Appraiser engaged through the AMC (CORE-VAL-01); third-party draw inspections (CORE-SVC-05); licensed, insured contractor and third-party cost review on ground-up (RES-GU-10).
rows.policy_gap: No rule bans or discloses a related-party contractor on rehab loans. Ask the owner.

mcq.stem: Exhibit: a state business-entity record showing Maple Run's general contractor is managed by Sam Okafor. What is the strongest response?
mcq.key: Flag the related party, require third-party inspection before each draw, and refer the gap to a credit officer.
distractors: No issue; related contractors save cost.
Release draws on the contractor's own invoices.
Decline the loan automatically under policy.

red_flags: Draw requests for work not in place
Photos reused or not of the subject
Missing or unsigned lien waivers
Subcontractor complaints or mechanics' liens
documents: Third-party inspection report with dated photos
rows.control: Inspection of work in place; conditional waivers for this draw and unconditional for the last; date-down with no new liens; loan in balance (CORE-SVC-05); reimbursement only, one draw per 30 days, 10% held to completion (RES-FF-09).

mcq.stem: Exhibit: Maple Run month-8 draw. The roof is 60% done but billed at 100%. Last draw's unconditional waiver is missing. What may be released?
mcq.key: Nothing until the missing waiver arrives; then only work in place (CORE-SVC-05).
distractors: The full request, since the budget allows it.
60% of the roof line now.
The full request, holding back 10%.

red_flags: Changed wire instructions
New or look-alike email domain or phone number
Rush to fund early or skip a step
Payee name not the CPL agent's escrow account
rows.control: CPL in hand (CORE-CLS-02); callback to a number already on file, never one from the request; stop-and-verify flags hold the wire (CORE-KYC-07); dual control and receipt confirmation (CORE-CLS-03).

mcq.stem: Exhibit: an email from 'title-agency-closings.co' on funding day with new wire instructions and a phone number to confirm. What does policy require?
mcq.key: Hold the wire and call the agent on the number already on file (CORE-KYC-07; CORE-CLS-03).
distractors: Call the number in the email to confirm.
Wire to the new account; the CPL covers it.
Reply to the email asking if it is genuine.

red_flags: Second lender's mortgage or deed of trust recorded after ours
Borrower refinancing the same asset elsewhere
UCC filings by another lender on rents or fixtures
Title date-down shows new liens
documents: Recorded security instrument and assignment of rents
rows.control: Title commitment with lender's policy (CORE-CLS-01); trailing documents logged and chased (CORE-CLS-05); date-down at each draw (CORE-SVC-05).
rows.policy_gap: No rule requires a UCC search at origination, or a periodic lien search on loans with no draws. Ask the owner.

mcq.stem: Exhibit: a Birchwood title date-down at month 6 shows a $400,000 mortgage to another lender. What does this most likely show?
mcq.key: A second pledge of our collateral, which is likely a default under the loan documents.
distractors: A routine tax lien.
Our own recording, filed twice.
A mechanics' lien from the capex work.

red_flags: Vacant land or a free-and-clear property
Seller reachable only by email or text, often out of state
Price below market and a rush to close
Seller asks for proceeds by wire to a new account
documents: Settlement statement and seller proceeds instructions
rows.control: Title commitment with lender's policy (CORE-CLS-01); closing agent under a closing protection letter (CORE-CLS-02); callback and stop-and-verify flags on any wire (CORE-KYC-07; CORE-CLS-03)
rows.policy_gap: No rule requires the lender to confirm the seller's identity on a purchase. Ask the owner.

mcq.stem: Fictional what-if: a free-and-clear lot whose 'seller' signs remotely, wants a quick close and asks for proceeds to a new overseas account. What is the strongest response?
mcq.key: Treat it as possible seller impersonation: hold closing and ask the title agent to verify the owner's identity.
distractors: Close, because title insurance covers every forgery loss.
Close, but wire the proceeds in two parts.
Close, once the buyer confirms the seller by email.

rows.typology: Dual contracts or undisclosed seller credits
red_flags: Two versions of the purchase contract
Seller credits on the settlement statement that are not in the contract
Price raised with a matching credit back to the buyer
Large assignment fee to a related party
rows.control: Value is the lower of price and appraised value (F-CORE-14); the wire must tie to the settlement statement (F-CORE-41; CORE-CLS-03); conflicting documents stop the file (CORE-KYC-07)
rows.policy_gap: No rule nets seller credits from price or caps them. Ask the owner; no limit is set here.

mcq.stem: Fictional what-if: the contract says $300,000, and the settlement statement shows a $30,000 seller credit not in the contract. What does this most likely show?
mcq.key: A dual contract or hidden credit that overstates the price and the borrower's equity.
distractors: A routine closing-cost credit that needs no review.
An appraisal error that the desk review will fix.
A title charge the closing agent forgot to list.

what_to_look_up_yourself: Read FinCEN advisory FIN-2012-A009 and FIN-2019-A005 for each red-flag family.
Read the FBI IC3 2025 annual report for current real estate and BEC loss figures.
Ask the owner to decide the three policy gaps: direct bank verification, related-party contractors, UCC and lien searches.
Look for FinCEN or FBI material on seller impersonation of vacant and free-and-clear property (FRD-11).
Ask the owner to decide the two new policy gaps: seller identity on purchases (FRD-11) and seller credits (FRD-12).
how_to_check_it: Check that the ten quality bar 11.3 typologies, FRD-11 and FRD-12 each have a row with a document, an outcome and an MCQ idea.
Look up each policy rule ID in the Model Credit Policy and confirm it says what the control column claims.
For any row, confirm each DOC ID exists in `document-registry.json` and lists this typology.
